title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
summary: Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards. Deployed systems face persistent shift, delayed dependent feedback, correlated component failures, and costly architecture changes. We formalize meta-agent architecture search as sequential incumbent replacement with switching costs and hard risk constraints and introduce Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS). CMAS retrieves archived architectures and proposes typed graph edits, then scores each against the incumbent by paired shadow replay under common random numbers, with interventional component credit. Promotion requires an empirically calibrated, variance-penalized simultaneous score above a pre-specified margin, and is followed by a simulated canary stage and pre-specified rollback. Since backtests cannot certify meta-level skill, we introduce MetaInvest-Bench, a regime-switching simulator whose specified worker competence makes a surrogate-optimal architecture computable, with leakage-controlled replay, adversarial governance tracks, and five negative controls. Financial streams serve as a risk-sensitive testbed for meta-level generalization; we claim no alpha. Across 96 streams, CMAS cuts normalized mean surrogate dynamic-oracle regret from 0.116 to 0.104 and raises held-out utility from 0.44 to 0.48 over the strongest adaptive baseline; when extra workers add no value, it contracts to near-single-agent teams. Its deployment inference cost is ~6% lower, though its search-inclusive token cost is the highest of the methods compared. The observed per-update false-promotion rate is 3.4% against a nominal 5% target, and 4.8% in a sealed rerun. The calibration is empirical: it concerns an update-level replay statistic on an author-designed benchmark, and guarantees neither full-utility improvement, nor absence of simulated canary-stage harm, nor sequence-level error control.

title: Evaluating the Applicability of LLM Inference Optimizations on Apple Silicon
summary: Apple Silicon is among the most widely used platforms for local LLM inference, yet nearly all inference optimizations are designed and validated on server-class NVIDIA GPUs under batched serving workloads. Which optimizations retain their benefits when moved to Apple Silicon, and what determines their applicability? We evaluate four optimization families: KV-cache pruning, speculative decoding, ported GPU kernels, and post-training quantization. Experiments span four Apple machines under a common single-request decode workload, with matched RTX 4090 comparisons where possible. KV-cache pruning can reach up to 1.75 times end-to-end throughput on Apple but can reduce throughput on desktop NVIDIA GPUs. Under the common benchmark, all evaluated speculative decoding methods reduce throughput on Apple, despite reported 2-6 times gains on server GPUs. CUDA kernel designs transfer only partially: public Metal lacks asynchronous copy, and batch-one decode makes several serving-oriented mechanisms inapplicable, although transferable components yield up to 1.20 times decode throughput. Quantization gains vary by machine. Across four families, a reported speedup is not a portable property of a technique alone but a joint function of technique, runtime, hardware contract, and workload regime.

title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
summary: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.

title: claude-code v2.1.304
summary:
What's changed

  • Added a transcript line when a plugin that runs first skips one of your mod's hooks, naming the event and the plugin
  • Added decider: "person" to a mod's tool.check answer: only the permission dialog or a host's callback can approve the ask, and it is refused with the mod's reason where nobody can be asked
  • Added e.isReadOnly to a mod's tool.check event, set when the tool call is read-only
  • Added /auto-mode-setup: a guided setup that reads your project and recent sessions to teach auto mode about your environment, now also available on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Claude apps gateway and telemetry-disabled sessions
  • Added /claude-api managed-agents-secure, which compares a Managed Agents agent's settings with Anthropic's published security guide, without changing anything
  • Added the names of the tools called earlier to the compaction summary in the transcript view (Ctrl+O)
  • Added a warning on Pro and Max plans when resuming an inactive conversation would use a noticeable share of your 5-hour usage limit: resume anyway, or start a new conversation and Claude can look up the previous one if you refer to it
  • Fixed the organization policy not refreshing until the hourly check after approving an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at startup or switching "Use custom API key" in /config
  • Fixed sandboxed commands failing to start on Linux when a sandbox.filesystem.denyRead glob contains brackets that are not a character class, such as a [user-id] route folder
  • Fixed rm -r of a mounted drive or a folder at its top level (/Volumes, /media, WSL's /mnt/c) not getting the safety prompt that rm -rf /Applications gets
  • Fixed CLAUDE_CODE_TRANSCRIPT_LOCAL_GC dropping messages from the saved transcript when the disk filled up while the file was being trimmed
  • Fixed a plugin keeping a headless run going past --max-turns, Stop, or ended input by spawning subagents or re-running a finished one
  • Fixed a failed mod reload removing the tools and commands of the version that stays loaded, and its messages being wrong or silent about whether the previous version is still loaded
  • Fixed a click on a mod's button being lost when buttons with the same label and no key were redrawn unchanged
  • Fixed mod sharing in the built-in plugin-authoring skill stopping at the secret scan on machines with managed settings and on Team and Enterprise plans
  • Fixed scheduled Cowork cloud sessions waiting five minutes again for each subagent whose WebFetch needed a URL approval that nobody was there to give
  • Fixed Write results and rejected edits showing a file outside the working directory as ../../…; they now show ~/… or the full path
  • Fixed a claude.ai Directory plugin's skills not running as commands when picked from the "/" menu in Cowork cloud sessions
  • Fixed Remote Control permanently withholding a desktop conversation's history when a different account was signed in to the terminal
  • Fixed Remote Control failing to start from Claude Desktop when DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK is set on a paid plan
  • Fixed model switches, messages and interrupts waiting behind a context usage check in SDK and desktop sessions
  • Fixed context_management: Extra inputs are not permitted errors behind LLM gateways; Claude Code now resends the request without that field
  • Fixed OpenTelemetry settings delivered through server-managed settings being ignored for the whole session after signing in during first-run setup or the first start after /logout
  • Fixed unsandboxed Bash commands in Claude Desktop Code tab sessions on macOS and Linux not seeing environment variables exported in shell startup files such as ~/.zshrc
  • Fixed the Consumer Terms notice being skipped for a day or longer after a server error
  • Fixed /privacy-settings offering choices that may not apply to you after a network or server error
  • Fixed a "Context limit reached" or "Prompt is too long" error after stopping a turn while Claude Code was compacting a conversation the API had rejected as too long
  • Fixed subagents sometimes forgetting their most recent work when they were messaged or resumed right after finishing
  • Fixed claude --help text for --tools, --resume, --debug, --json-schema, --disable-slash-commands, --system-prompt-snapshot and claude update to match actual behavior
  • Fixed claude --worktree removing the worktree and its branch without asking at exit when HEAD was detached or on another branch, which could lose commits
  • Fixed resumed and cloud sessions sending Claude the whole skill list again each time plugins reloaded at startup
  • Fixed an interrupt not ending a Read that waits on an idle pipe or device named like an image
  • Fixed /effort status, /effort ultracode and the prompt's effort indicator showing a guessed effort level when CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is auto or unset and no level is sent
  • Fixed a PreToolUse hook's deny reason being replaced by a timeout error when an Agent SDK callback hook on the same tool call timed out
  • Fixed Bash and PowerShell deleting a large command's output file when it could not be copied to the session's tool-results folder, unless the disk is full
  • Fixed notes typed into a multiple-choice question with previews being cut off with "…" in terminals under about 100 columns, hiding what was typed (#82768)
  • Fixed self-paced /loop wakeups scheduled at the 1-hour maximum firing just after the 1-hour prompt cache expired, so those wakeups no longer re-read the conversation uncached
  • Fixed agent teams: approving a shutdown request from the main session no longer exits the whole CLI
  • Fixed a skill's once hook also removing another skill's identical hook after it ran
  • Fixed transcript mode's { and } landing the prompt on an inconsistent row, or off screen, instead of the transcript's first row
  • Fixed CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200k silently setting a 100K window: the variable now accepts k and M suffixes like --autocompact, and warns when a value is out of range or ignored
  • Fixed Ctrl+C in the agents view clearing a text selection without copying it when pressed before the mouse button was released
  • Improved /usage to say when a rate limit on usage data ends instead of "try again in a moment"
  • Improved the lines shown when a mod written in the session loads, reloads or fails to load
  • Improved artifacts with several views: when you ask for links to them, Claude now writes out each view's link and explains that the address bar stays the same as you switch views
  • Improved cloud sessions: a new conversation's first turn no longer waits for the local (stdio) MCP servers of plugins synced from claude.ai, unless a server sets alwaysLoad: true
  • Improved how a remote session recovers its status when the server refuses a status update that carried other session data
  • Improved session file size in auto mode: the safety classifier's context is no longer stored with every request
  • Improved the claude -p invalid-settings warning: a file that did not load lists only what stopped it, and long lists are capped per file
  • Improved resume of large compacted sessions in SDK and headless mode: the first request after resuming is sent sooner
  • Improved responsiveness and throughput when many subagents are running at the same time
  • Improved memory use when sending requests in long or resumed conversations
  • Self-hosted runner: Improved the error shown when the git host answers "not found" for a session's repository: it now names the repository and whom to ask
  • Windows: Improved git command start-up with a standard Git for Windows install by running its git.exe directly instead of through its cmd launcher
  • Changed mods' settings.read hooks to receive each settings layer and rewrite the merged settings, so a managed mod can make an organization's setting a ceiling, including the cleanupPeriodDays the retention sweep uses
  • Changed the /artifacts delete confirmation to show numbered choices: 1 or Enter keeps the artifact, 2 deletes it, and y, n and Esc still work
  • Changed the question that turns on the mods Claude writes in a session to plain text with no link or session id; it stays up when a new turn starts, and Claude tells you what loaded when you turn them on
  • Changed tool search to be on by default behind a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; a 400 or 422 from the gateway is retried without it
  • Changed compaction to send Claude the skill list again afterwards; /reload-skills now sends only new or changed skills
  • Changed skill hooks: the skills of one source (a repo, your own folder, or a plugin) can register at most 1,024 hooks and 16,384 matcher characters per session
  • Changed skills under a policy that allows hooks from plugins only: a skill used in the main conversation whose hooks are kept out no longer gets its allowed-tools
  • Updated the /claude-api skill to use the ant CLI on Claude Platform on AWS instead of falling back to the SDK or curl
  • Removed the notes from claude plugin validate that predicted where a mod's hooks would run
  • Removed the "(research preview)" label from the /fast dialog title on Opus 5.5
  • [VSCode] Added mod drawing in the chat panel for sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, behind an LLM gateway, or with telemetry turned off
  • [VSCode] Fixed one cause of sessions failing to start with "Subprocess initialization did not complete within 60000ms": time a SessionStart command hook spends running no longer counts toward the limit, up to 10 minutes in total
  • [VSCode] Fixed a session closed while it was starting keeping its Claude Code process running until the start ended
  • [VSCode] Fixed a mod's drawings disappearing from a long-open panel until the next turn on machines that also run an older Claude Code
  • [VSCode] Fixed Past conversations hiding sessions when claudeCode.claudeProcessWrapper is set
  • [VSCode] Changed background sub-agents to show as one status line under their Agent card instead of streaming every step into the chat; the full transcript stays in /tasks
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed folders in the composer's @ list showing no name in cloud sessions, where picking one added only a space instead of a mention
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude going silent in a thread when its channel becomes shared across Enterprise Grid workspaces mid-task; it now posts a one-time note to @-mention it in a new thread
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed @Claude !fork typed outside a thread getting no visible reply; Claude now shows you a private note saying to run it from inside a thread
  • [Code Review] Added review levels to Code Review: Owners choose Quick, Standard (the default), or Deep for the organization, and can give individual repositories their own level
  • [Code Review] Added an option in Code Review admin settings to review every repository in a GitHub organization, including ones added later, without selecting them one by one
  • [Code Review] Fixed pull requests opened within a minute or two of an admin turning on Code Review being silently skipped; they are now retried and reviewed

title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
summary: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.

title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
summary: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.

title: vllm v0.32.0
summary:
v0.32.0

Highlights

This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)!

  • Structured decisions and generic parsers: the new POST /v1/systemone endpoint answers choice, noul and score questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on Cloudflare/clef-omni (#61064), LiquidAI/d1-3B (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new hf tool and reasoning parser (--tool-call-parser hf, --reasoning-parser hf) reads the checkpoint's response_template, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005).
  • Low-precision KV cache everywhere: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); fp8_ds_mla on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit ultraquant_4bit KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057).
  • Model Runner V2: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360).
  • Faster startup and serving: vllm download-kernels installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); vllm preload --preload-autotune keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with --api-server-count above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in the PR's benchmark (#60723).
  • Model support: new EmbeddingGemma 2 omni-modal embeddings (#60254), MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674) and Nemotron 3.5 ASR (#59827); video input in the Transformers modeling backend (#57441); GLM-5.3 sparse MLA index conversions reused across layers (3.5-3.9x on that kernel, #59464) and fused multi-step draft decode (13.3% at concurrency 1, #57443); HiSparse per-request residency caching for up to 58% more throughput on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200 with long, fully GPU-resident contexts at high concurrency (#60083).
  • Security: fixes for GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (chat template resource exhaustion, #50300), GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4 (tokenizer max_token_id, #59491) and GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9 (P2P ZMQ socket exhaustion, #51504); CORS no longer allows every origin by default (#61009); untrusted images are limited to raster formats (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are signed (#59357); and JSON schemas nested deeper than 64 levels are rejected (#60036).
  • Breaking changes: Python 3.10 dropped (#60402); default CORS origins restricted (#61009); transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 (#57387, #59796); torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes removed (#60517); cascade attention removed (#61126); mamba_cache_mode="all" removed (#58997); max_tokens no longer reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API reasoning stream events renamed (#59652).

  • Source distribution tarball

Model Support

  • New models: EmbeddingGemma 2 (google/embeddinggemma-2), an omni-modal text/image/audio/video embedding model, with unused modality encoders skipped through --limit-mm-per-prompt (#60254, #60289); MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674); Nemotron 3.5 ASR (nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b) complete-audio transcription; native realtime streaming is not yet supported (#59827); Cloudflare/clef-omni (#61064) and LiquidAI/d1-3B (#60676) on /v1/systemone; PLaMo 3 reasoning and tool parsers (#56575); and the zerank-2 reranker score template (#60415).
  • Transformers modeling backend: video inputs (#57441), and Glm, Arcee, CWM, Mellum (#59679), GPT-NeoX, Phi, Seed-OSS and Jais2 (#59701) now served through it.
  • New model capabilities: LoRA for BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-RoBERTa embedding models (#61033); Granite as an EAGLE3/DFlash target (#60855); Qwen3-ASR EAGLE3 (#52824); Sarvam MLA EAGLE3/DSpark with PP (#55902); GLM-5.3-Flash with the DFlash2 drafter (#56983); and MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 at PP > 1 on MRV2 (#57197) with MTP sharing target embeddings under PP (#58648).

  • Qwen: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) merged QSA projections in one GEMM (1.45-1.68x, #59533), fused QSA pre-indexer (#57097), sequence parallelism through --enable-hc-sp (#56322), SM100 low-latency decode GEMM plans (up to 2.7x vs cuBLAS on small-M, #59214), --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers honored (#60023), and PLE loading for INC (#59990), Quark (#59443) and pre-SM89 GPUs (#60142); Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 M-RoPE cache 4x smaller and Qwen3.5 YaRN matching Transformers (#59853); Qwen3-Omni M-RoPE fixes (#58890, #59842); Qwen3-ASR on the upstream processor (#57146); Qwen3-VL unknown video fps (#60501) and per-video options with the multimodal cache (#55203).

  • Model Runner V2: GPU n-gram speculator (#40704), Elastic EP with drain-then-commit scaling (#53934), PP with PCP for MLA models (#59139), STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE mode (#59079), dynamic K in autoregressive speculators (#57053), MTP sampling-mask replay (#59359) and per-module LM heads (#58921), non-blocking H2D copies on WSL2 (#60215), and fixes for int64 index offsets at long context (#60736), warmup (#61013), GDN prefill checkpoints (#59536) and MRV2+PP+MTP align state (#60210).

Security

  • GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7: chat templates are validated statically and rendered under a timeout (VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT), user-supplied chat_template in Responses chat_template_kwargs is rejected, and the Rust frontend caps template execution (#50300).
  • GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4: tokenizer max_token_id off-by-one fixed (#59491).
  • GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9: P2P ZMQ peer sessions are bounded by VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS (default 128), VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30) and VLLM_P2P_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S (default 300), so unique peer addresses can no longer exhaust ZMQ sockets (#51504).
  • Default CORS settings no longer allow every origin in the Python and Rust frontends; set --allowed-origins to permit browser origins (#61009).
  • Untrusted images are opened with a raster-format allowlist (ALLOWED_IMAGE_FORMATS), denying EPS/PostScript and WMF (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are HMAC-signed and forged handles rejected (#59357).
  • Structured-output JSON schemas nested more than 64 levels return 400 (#60036); chunked /v1/embeddings requests keep cache_salt (#47696); Phi-4 MM audio no longer holds multi-GiB attention matrices (#60614); DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum pixel tensors no longer kill EngineCore (#59417).
  • Security dependency bumps: aiohttp>=3.14.3, pillow>=12.3.0, cryptography, urllib3, pyjwt and others (#59249, #59315, #59427).

  • transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 (minimum raised from 5.10.4, #57387, #59762) and tokenizers>=0.23.2 (#59796).

Build

  • Python 3.11-3.14 supported (#60402); macOS wheels built with the stable ABI (#60312); CUDA source builds require GCC 13 and fail early otherwise (#60259); Docker images compile Python bytecode at build time for faster container startup (#55422); VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED finds a compatible published wheel within the last 20 commits (#58871); the vendored DeepGEMM uses TORCH_LIBRARY (abi3, #48962).

Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Python 3.10 is no longer supported; the minimum is Python 3.11 (#60402).
  • Default CORS origins changed from * to none; set --allowed-origins for browser clients (#61009).
  • transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 are required (#57387, #59796).
  • The torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes were removed, along with PassConfig.enable_sp, fuse_gemm_comms and sp_min_token_num; model-level sequence parallelism is unaffected (#60517).
  • Cascade attention was removed; --disable-cascade-attn still parses but only warns and will be removed in v0.33.0 (#61126).
  • mamba_cache_mode="all" was removed; --mamba-cache-mode all now fails validation (#58997).
  • Previously deprecated APIs were removed: wait_for_inflight_requests (use mode="wait"), AsyncLLM.pause_generation(), IOProcessor.output_to_response, vllm.scripts.main() and vllm bench throughput --dataset (#60923). The sonnet benchmark dataset was removed as scheduled (#60129). Tensorizer support was removed from LoRA (#60024), and the PyO3 vllm._rust_tool_parser bridge was removed (#59744).
  • API changes: max_tokens is treated as an upper bound on output rather than reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API streaming uses response.content_part.added/done with part.type="reasoning_text" instead of response.reasoning_part.added/done (#59652); SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids is per row (#56984); /inference/v1/generate logprobs use integer token IDs (#58181); sleep API responses are standardized and invalid levels return 400 (#52864); return_mm_kwargs is deprecated in favor of mm_payload (#61427).
  • Watermarking: when the engine has watermarking configured, an omitted request field means enabled and only false opts out; unsupported combinations warn and fall back (#56801).
  • Rust frontend: qwen3_xml now parses Qwen3-Coder XML (alias of qwen3_coder); use the new qwen3_json for the JSON format (#60136).
  • New defaults: shared-memory tensor arena on (#51207); GLM-5.x FP8 KV cache on SM100 with --kv-cache-dtype auto (#60140, #60281); VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE=1 (#57991); Humming preferred over Marlin on SM90 (#56997); sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor 2 above 256K max_model_len (#61023); MRV2 on ROCm with model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360); VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=auto (#59965); dtype=auto picks bfloat16 on PowerPC (#58528); MXFP4 W4A4 checkpoints fall back to W4A16 with a warning when no W4A4 kernel exists (#60079).
  • Stricter validation: incompatible --prefix-match-unit (#58021), max_num_scheduled_tokens=0 (#60714), HiSparse with cudagraph_mode=FULL (#59688), and negative --device-ids (#49053) are rejected at startup.

title: Expanding Claude availability and deployment choice on Google Cloud
summary:
Every organization has unique requirements for building and scaling generative AI. At Google Cloud, we are committed to giving developers model choice and architectural flexibility to run workloads however they need.

Today, we’re announcing the general availability of an Anthropic-managed deployment option for Claude Models on Google Cloud. This gives teams more choice in how they run their models, helping them consolidate AI workloads on Google Cloud alongside our existingGoogle-managed deployment option. 

Both options deliver the same frontier models on day zero, the same pricing, and the same Google Cloud billing. The difference comes down to who acts as your data processor and whether you need access to the new Claude platform features when they launch:

[NEW] Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)

Delivers day-zero access to Claude models and Claude Platform features such as Claude Managed Agents (beta), skills, and code execution. Anthropic operates the stack as the data processor on Google Cloud infrastructure under Anthropic’s terms of service, while organizations authenticate with Google Cloud IAM, maintain Cloud Audit Logging, and consolidate spend under their existing Google Cloud billing and eligible commitments.

Learn more: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic-managed).

Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)

Continues to deliver day-zero access to the latest Claude models with strict governance, compliance, and sovereignty requirements. Google Cloud operates as the data processor under existing customer agreements, providing VPC Service Controls, Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK), and data residency in the U.S., EU, and APAC. New Claude Platform features roll out over time as they are integrated into the Google-managed infrastructure. Teams also benefit from native integrations with Google Cloud services like BigQuery and Model Armor, along with standard billing and eligible commitment drawdown. 

Learn more: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)

Comparing deployment options

 

Feature

Anthropic-managed

Google-managed

Model availability

Available on Day 0

Available on Day 0

First-party tools and betas 

Available on Day 0

Available once integrated into the Google-managed infrastructure

Data processor and terms

Anthropic (under Anthropic’s Commercial Terms)

Google Cloud (under existing Google Cloud customer agreements)

Pricing & commitments

Standard pricing (draws down eligible Google Cloud commitments)

No matter how you choose to deploy, you can access Anthropic's latest frontier models on Google Cloud, including Claude Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Opus 5.5, with new platform features available immediately on the Anthropic-managed option and rolling out on the Google-managed option once integrated. This gives developers the full spectrum of reasoning, coding, and multi-modal capabilities with Google Cloud IAM and Marketplace billing. Get started.
